title: The dietary effects of xanthan gum in man
authors: Eastwood MA, Brydon WG, Anderson DM
followUp: 23 consecutive days after a 7-day control period
population: Five healthy men aged 26 to 50 years, body weight 69 to 78 kg
funder: not readable. The full text is behind a paywall and no open copy was located; the PubMed record lists no grant support and indexes the paper as Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't.
result: Each man consumed 15 times the then acceptable daily intake of 10 mg/kg body weight: the lightest and heaviest took 10.4 and 12.9 g of xanthan gum per day, as a pre-hydrated gel, on each of 23 consecutive days. Faecal wet and dry weight rose and intestinal transit time fell. Serum cholesterol was 10% lower and faecal bile acid concentrations were higher (both p < 0.05 as reported by EFSA). Plasma biochemistry, haematological indices, urinalysis, glucose tolerance and insulin tests, serum immunoglobulins, triglycerides, phospholipids, HDL cholesterol and breath hydrogen and methane did not change significantly. Numbers were read in the PubMed abstract and in the EFSA 2017 re-evaluation, which converts the dose to 149 to 184 mg/kg body weight per day for a 70 kg adult.
